text: So I booked this hotel for my family's last night in Morocco before leaving the next day to return to America after visiting my husband and I in Taza. So my standards aren't very high when it comes to hotels etc as I have slept and ate in some crappy places. This hotel on the surface appears very nice. motels the reason the bed frame goes all the way to the floor is to make the room easier to clean - so maids don't have to kneel down and search under beds to see if the last occupant had left a empty water bottle and perfume bottle under the bed. In this case in this hotel - the beds are on these plastic and wooden slatted platforms with a lot of empty space for trash to collect - if maids aren't diligent if they are lazy and don't want to pick up the trash under the bed. I also noticed as did my mother that it was HOT in the rooms. We tried to turn on the thermostat in both rooms So then my mother called the front desk asking them how to work the thermostat because it didn't seem to be working - As the Ibis Hotel Chain which is owned by Accor Hotels states 15 minutes to fix problems - it was on the flyer in the room. They sent a guy up to her room - he looked at the thermostat - then asked if they speak French - no we are Americans and its their first trip to Africa - no they don't speak French and then leaves. A few minutes later the front desk calls and says that "At this time of year the thermostat is not turned on Well this is weird and frustrating to me and my family considering all the materials throughout this hotel's media and advertisment is talking about how it wants you to have the best night's sleep possible. Why even put individual thermostats in the rooms if your not going to let the guests use them? I can't sleep when its hot in my bedroom - neither can my husband It was Hammam hot hot and humid - in both our rooms and we couldn't turn the AC on at all! We went downstairs and tried to go to the restuarant - which in the elevator is advertised to be open until 11pm - we arrived at 10:30pm and were turned away - told quite curtly by a waitress they were closed - they told us go to the bar and order from the other menu there. So we ordered at bar in which we were told only two entree's on the menu were avalible quiche and chicken panini. I personally think its pretty shameful such a large chain hotel ran out of 24 entrees listed on the menu - I wondered if the Ibis hotels have a supply chain issue when it comes to food items - which given there is one everyone else in my family ordered the chicken panini - which turned out to be a complete joke - there was no chicken in fact it was SO lacking chicken that my mother said - I guess this is a mayo panini hold the chicken. The hotel also had this strange perfume throughout all the common areas such as halls bars and reception that I ended up sneezing at every time I left our room. Back to the thermostat issues - so we had thought that our hot rooms would be solved by opening the windows - which did reduce the temperature My husband is such a light sleeper that each time one buzzed near his ear - he woke up. The noise pollution from outside our hotel with the window open would have kept me up We got breakfast down stairs - which was the only high light of the stay besides the parking for our rented car and the shower in my mother's room. I wouldn't recommend staying here to anyone else after our stay and from a PCV that is saying something especially at this price point in Morocco
